title: memory-fragmentation-oom-root-cause-investigation-notes-v5
content:
Summary:

This doc collects notes and experiment results from the serving-runtime team investigating recurring OOMs in long-running Dedicated pools and a small number of Hosted customers. Root causes appear to be a mix of allocator behavior (external fragmentation), frequent small cudaMalloc/cudaFree churn, and conservative workspace sizing formulas that leave little headroom when fragmentation accumulates.

Symptoms observed:
- Out-of-memory crashes on long-lived GPU processes after several hours of steady traffic (not tied to a single large request).
- Memory footprint slowly increases in steps rather than linearly; free memory reported by nvidia-smi is fragmented (small holes).
- Reproduced more reliably under continuous-batched workloads with variable sequence lengths and frequent model switches.
- When we trigger a model reload or restart, GPU memory is reclaimed — suggests in-process fragmentation vs kernel/driver leak.

Initial hypotheses:
1) CUDA allocator (cudaMalloc) fragmentation: repeated allocations of varying sizes lead to holes that cannot satisfy larger workspace allocations.
2) Host allocator / GPU memory pool mismatch: our custom pool + per-request workspace allocation logic interacts poorly with jemalloc/tcmalloc rounding, causing mismatched sizes and internal fragmentation.
3) Workspace sizing too tight: we compute workspace sizes based on median sequence length and rarely allocate headroom, so a burst of larger sequences can trigger OOM if fragmented.
4) KV-cache growth and eviction timing: some models keep KV cache pinned and we delay eviction, increasing pressure.

What we profiled / how:
- nvprof / Nsight Systems traces on a slow repro run to capture cudaMalloc/cudaFree hotspots. Commands: 
  - nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx -o run-2026-03-03.qdrep 
  - cudaMalloc/cudaFree call counters instrumented via allocator wrapper logs (see debug build).
- Heap / pool snapshots (custom): we added a debug endpoint to dump pool buckets, free lists, and total used vs reserved.
- nvidia-smi loop capturing free memory and process reports every 5s.
- Perf counters for kernel time vs memcpy to rule out driver leaks.

Key findings:
- High frequency of small allocations: ~70% of allocations are < 64KB and many are transient (life < 50ms). These cause many small free segments.
- Our initial allocator (simple buddy-like pool with power-of-two buckets) fails under mixed-size patterns: bucket rounding causes internal fragmentation and leaves free segments that are too small for later medium-size workspace reqs.
- cudaMalloc is relatively expensive under heavy churn; we observed spikes in latency tied to synchronous cudaMalloc calls. Sometimes cudaMalloc falls back to driver-level allocation causing large contiguous regions to be requested and fail when fragmentation exists.
- Workspace allocation pattern: for token generation we allocate a contiguous workspace per request (for attention scratch, FFN buffers). Some of these allocations are sized according to a formula that uses expected max_seq + kv_cache_size + safety_margin. The safety_margin was set low (5–10%) to optimize for utilization. With fragmentation, margin is insufficient.
- CUDA memory is not compactable in-process. So once fragmentation occurs, only a full restart releases contiguous ranges.

Experiments run and outcomes:
1) Pre-allocate big arena at startup and sub-allocate from it (fixed pool):
   - Implemented prototype that calls a single big cudaMalloc chunk per worker (configurable, e.g., 80% of free GPU). Sub-allocs come from this arena.
   - Result: fragmentation reduced dramatically for mixed-size allocations; OOMs didn't reproduce in 12h stress test.
   - Tradeoff: less memory available to other processes; risk of over-committing on multi-tenant nodes.
2) Batch allocation + reuse for transient buffers:
   - Reuse per-thread scratch buffers instead of allocating per-request. Simple thread-local cache for typical sizes.
   - Result: number of small cudaMalloc calls dropped by ~80%, latency improved for small requests.
3) Increase safety margin for workspace sizing:
   - Increased margin from 10% -> 30% for models with high variability. Reduced OOMs but increased average resident footprint ~12%.
4) Eviction tweaks for KV cache:
   - Aggressively evicted KV cache for long-idle sessions. Reduced pressure but did not fully eliminate fragmentation issue.
5) jemalloc arena tuning on host:
   - Adjusted host allocator settings to reduce memory stampeding and to align GPU pinned allocations to larger pages. Had marginal benefit.

Root cause (synthesized):
- Primary: allocator-induced external fragmentation due to many small transient allocations and bucket rounding. The allocator plus cudaMalloc interaction results in holes that block larger contiguous workspace allocations.
- Secondary: workspace sizing optimized for utilization (small safety margin) exacerbates the issue — once holes appear there is insufficient contiguous region to satisfy a large workspace and cudaMalloc fails.
- Tertiary: kube/OS-level co-tenancy can amplify impact when multiple processes allocate/deallocate, but the dominant issue is in-process fragmentation.

Short-term mitigations (low effort, quick rollouts):
- Patch: enable thread-local reusable scratch buffers for common sizes (PR: linked above). Roll out to Hosted first. Owner: Ben Carlson.
- Increase workspace safety margin for models flagged as high-variance (config feature toggle). Owner: Lina Martinez.
- Add better debug telemetry: record fragmentation metrics (largest_free_block, free_block_count, bucket_histogram) for each worker every minute. Owner: Aisha Patel.

Medium-term fixes (requires testing):
- Arena-based allocator by default with conservative growth strategy: allocate a large contiguous arena per worker and sub-allocate. Provide knob for percent_of_gpu. Pros: eliminates cudaMalloc churn and fragmentation within arena. Cons: loses flexibility for multi-tenant nodes. Implementation owner: Jungsoo Kim.
- Smart workspace sizing algorithm: use historical seq-length distribution + p99 headroom instead of median. Add adaptive per-runtime resizing when fragmentation observed. Implementation owner: Lina Martinez + perf team.
- Opportunistic restart policy: when fragmentation metrics exceed thresholds (largest_free_block < needed_for_max_workspace AND free_block_count > X) perform graceful process recycle to compact memory. This is a practical fallback for Dedicated pools.

Longer-term / research items:
- Investigate CUDA memory defragmentation / CUDA 12+ features that allow memory compaction (if any). Currently not available for general users.
- Explore use of cudaMallocAsync (if driver on host supports) + async memory pool to reduce sync overhead. Caveat: requires driver and runtime support; behavior w.r.t fragmentation needs validation.
- Evaluate third-party GPU allocators (mimalloc-like for GPU) and community patterns (PyTorch caching allocator behavior) and whether we can re-use ideas.

Testing plan before rollout:
- Unit tests for allocator invariants (no double-free, correct sub-alloc counts).
- Integration stress test: 48h continuous-batched workload with mixed seq length and model switching. Compare metrics: cudaMalloc call rate, largest_free_block, resident set size, OOM counts.
- Canaries: deploy Arena allocator to one Dedicated pool (low-risk) and monitor for 72h. Gate: no increase in customer-reported latency and no OOMs.

Open action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Instrument fragmentation telemetry and ship to Console (Aisha, by 2026-03-10).
- [ ] Merge PR for thread-local scratch reuse (Ben, PR #872).
- [ ] Implement arena allocator prototype with percent_of_gpu knob, benchmark (Jungsoo, target 2026-03-18).
- [ ] Update workspace sizing heuristics to use p95/p99 based headroom and add per-model config flag (Lina).
- [ ] Add autoscale/restart rule for fragmentation thresholds (SRE + serving-runtime).

Notes / gotchas we observed:
- cudaMallocAsync shows promise in microbenchmarks, but on some driver versions we saw different fragmentation patterns; requires careful cross-driver testing.
- Pre-allocating huge arenas helps but is a blunt instrument: for Hosted API we may prefer hybrid approach (small arena + fallback to cudaMalloc).
- Some customers run very large models where arena pre-allocation might be infeasible; need a per-customer/default strategy.

Relevant logs / snippets:
- Example allocator dump (trimmed):
  total_reserved: 12.8GB
  resident: 11.9GB
  largest_free_block: 64MB
  free_block_count: 1432
  bucket_histogram: [0-4KB: 840, 4-64KB: 1320, 64-512KB: 220, 512KB-8MB: 12, >8MB: 1]

- Nsight trace showed frequent cudaMalloc calls at ~1200/sec during peak; after scratch reuse patch this dropped to ~240/sec.

Appendix: quick mitigation config knobs we can hotflip:
- runtime.env.ALLOC_SCRATCH_REUSE=true
- model.config.workspace_safety_margin=0.30 (per-model override)
- runtime.env.ARENA_PERCENT=0.0..0.85 (0 disables arena)

If you have additional repros or customer traces (stacktraces + nsys qdrep), attach them here and tag the doc.

-- Aisha
